codeReview.summary: Round-2 reassessment still finds the prior blocking findings unresolved in current repo state: the feature commit includes non-test runtime startup behavior changes, and runner shutdown does not guarantee in-flight transcription work is drained before Mongo teardown.

issues.description: The feature contract required lifecycle hardening without altering stable/dev startup behavior outside test mode, but this commit still wires runtime startup paths (`initializeRealtimeServer(server)` at line 196 and `startAudioTranscriptionRunner()` at line 216) in normal server boot. These remain out of scope for the assigned lifecycle-only fix.

`stopAudioTranscriptionRunner()` only clears `runnerHandle` and returns. It does not await an already-running `runAudioTranscriptionTick()` (line 525) or settle `activeJobs` (line 533 onward). Since interval ticks invoke `void runAudioTranscriptionTick()` (lines 568-569), queue work can continue after stop is called, so teardown is not guaranteed quiescent before Mongo disconnect.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Mission/repo guidance does not currently enforce a strict staged-diff scope gate for dirty-tree feature work, which allowed unrelated runtime deltas to be bundled into this lifecycle fix.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Commit 253aa75f includes broad `api/server/index.js` startup deltas while the feature definition in `features.json` scopes behavior to test/runtime lifecycle hardening and explicitly says not to alter stable/dev startup behavior outside test mode.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The backend-migration worker skill stresses minimal scoped changes but lacks an explicit pre-commit step requiring workers to prove staged files/lines only match feature intent when the worktree is already dirty.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Transcript skeleton for session `d2f31f5c-fdf0-4f1f-be0d-82034d1dcff6` shows the worker noticed `index.js` had a much larger diff than expected, yet the final commit still captured those runtime changes.

summary: Fail (round 2): both prior blockers remain in current state—out-of-scope runtime startup changes are still part of the feature commit, and transcription-runner shutdown still does not guarantee in-flight work is drained before Mongo teardown.
